## ghat-p03 — C1

**SUMMARY.** The rasa shifts from śṛṅgāra to vira/adbhuta: love and landscape are framed by the poet's skill, not by love alone. Clouds thundering make travelers long; sorrow grows, endless. Lovers honor the love-festival; cloud-arrival, dear friend, they bring. Then the tribute: may I be conquered by which poet, by yamakas; to him I pour water in ghaṭakarpara. The sthāyibhāva (love) resolves into the poet's own delight (camatkāra) at his craft. The potsherd is both vessel and namesake — the potsherd names itself at its close.

*Rasa: vira/adbhuta (heroic skill + wonder at craft), resolving from śṛṅgāra — The rasa shifts: the lover's voice yields to the poet's. The sthāyibhāva (love) transforms into the poet's delight at his own craft (camatkāra). The potsherd is both vessel and namesake. Flagged as application: Abhinava does not explicitly name this shift.*
